gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured steady-state power draw for any wheeled electric cooler. OutdoorGearLab measured the wheeled thermoelectric Igloo Iceless Versatemp 35 drawing 61.7 W and never getting colder than 43.7°F in a 75°F room. Under the same test, the wheeled compressor Anker Everfrost 40 held temperature on 5.8 W, about one tenth of that, and reached 1.4°F.
standout_why: Compared against GearJunkie (2026-10-31), giftsitter.com and lovethe88.com (wheels list). GearJunkie gives cool-down times and runtimes but no measured watts for any of its 9 coolers. It names an acoustic test but reports no dB figures. Its only wattage is a general 40–70 W range in the FAQ. Giftsitter and lovethe88 attribute every figure to 'supplied specifications' with no named tester. Giftsitter says thermoelectric units cool only '30–40°F below ambient', a spec claim with no wattage. Car and Driver's page could not be fetched (blocked) and Tom's Guide came back truncated, so neither was checked.
decides: It argues for a compressor cooler over the thermoelectric 'cooler/warmer' type. The Koolatron 33 qt card ChatGPT showed is that type, and ChatGPT added only that 'cooling performance depends on outside temperature.' In OutdoorGearLab's test, the wheeled thermoelectric Igloo used 370 Wh over 6 hours against 35 Wh for the wheeled Anker Everfrost 40, about 10.6×. The Igloo never reached 40°F, the usual food-safe line. That backs Dealectric's listed Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L, or another wheeled compressor unit, as the pick. Among those, Outdoor Life measured a Bodega QZW 48 reaching 0°F on 20 Wh, against 50 Wh for the Bluetti MultiCooler.
